sections.overview: Platyla polita is a tiny, operculate land snail with a broad but patchy European range.
sections.identification: Its smooth, glossy reddish-brown shell is elongated and tower-shaped, usually under 4 mm high.
sections.habitat: It lives in damp woodland litter, moss and decaying wood, often on moist, base-rich ground.
sections.diet: The species accounts consulted do not describe its diet in detail.
sections.behavior: It hides in litter and wood mould; in Latvia it is active in the growing season and overwinters below litter.
sections.reproduction: It has separate sexes; little else is known about its reproduction.
sections.ecology: In eastern France it also occurs under dead wood and among scree in cool deciduous forests.
sections.conservation: In 2023 Latvia assessed it as Vulnerable nationally, but Least Concern globally and in Europe.
